introductions.header: How to work with the administration

blocks.content: This manual guides you through the whole administration step by step. This introductory chapter explains how the administration is organised and how to use the elements you find on almost every page: the menu, tables, filters, forms, the trash, export, import and reports. Once you understand it, you will manage even pages you see for the first time.

Every admin page has a question-mark button at the top right of its header. It opens exactly the chapter of this manual that describes that page. The item Help at the bottom of the left menu (above Log out) opens the start of the manual - this page.

sections.heading: 01. What the administration is and what it consists of

blocks.content: The administration is the non-public part of the system where you manage the content and operation of all public applications - the website, the e-shop and the project portal for clients. Visitors do not see it and cannot get into it without an account.

cards.title: Core (system)
cards.text: The common base of all applications: user accounts, roles and permissions, legal documents, company details, the calendar, logs and security monitoring. Switch to Core with the Core tab in the header.

cards.title: Applications
cards.text: Separate parts of the system, for example Web, E-shop or Project portal. Each has its own menu, dashboard, logs and pages. Switch between applications with the Applications button in the header.

cards.title: Public part
cards.text: What visitors see - the website, the e-shop and the client portal. Most of what is shown there (texts, products, contacts, legal documents) is changed here in the administration.

cards.title: This manual
cards.text: The internal help. You only see the chapters for pages you have permission to. Chapters you miss describe pages your account cannot open.

blocks.highlight: What you see depends on your account
blocks.content: Every account has a role and possibly extra permissions. They decide which menu items, buttons and whole applications are shown. If something is missing in the administration or in the manual, it is not an error - your account lacks the permission. Ask the administrator who manages accounts to extend it (see the chapter Contacts and help).

steps.label: Activation e-mail
steps.text: An administrator creates your account. You receive an activation link by e-mail, valid for 48 hours.

steps.label: Setting the password
steps.text: The link opens a page where you choose your own password (8 to 64 characters, at least one letter, one digit and one special character). Nobody else knows the password - not even the administrator.

steps.label: Signing in
steps.text: On the sign-in page enter your e-mail and password. With two-factor authentication you also receive a six-digit code by e-mail.

steps.label: Welcome page
steps.text: After signing in the welcome page with your profile opens. If your account has no permission for it, the Access denied page is shown - continue from the left menu and ask the administrator for the permission of the welcome page (it is recommended for every account).

steps.label: Recommended first steps
steps.text: On the My account page check your name and e-mail, upload a profile photo and consider turning on two-factor authentication.

blocks.content: Details about signing in, passwords, two-factor authentication and how long a sign-in lasts are in the chapter Access and security.

The administration always has the same layout: the header at the top, the menu on the left and the page content in the middle. The header and the menu stay in place, only the page content scrolls. A long menu scrolls on its own.

cards.title: Menu button
cards.text: At the far left of the header. Hides or shows the left menu. The system remembers whether you left the menu open.

cards.title: Module name
cards.text: After the word Admin you see which module you are in (Core or the name of an application).

cards.title: Your account
cards.text: Profile photo, e-mail and role. Click it to open the account panel: My account, calendar, administration language and Log out.

cards.title: Clock
cards.text: Current date and time. Handy when working with times in the logs and the calendar.

cards.title: Module switcher
cards.text: A button with the name of the module you are in (Core or the name of an application). It opens a list: Core at the top (only with the permission for the Core section), the applications you have access to below a line, and All applications at the bottom - the overview of the applications with the state of each. The list works with the keyboard too (arrows, Escape).

blocks.content: The left menu is divided into sections (for example Overview, Content, Users, System). Click the name of a section to collapse or expand it - the system remembers it. Change the width of the menu by dragging its right edge with the mouse. At the very bottom of the menu of every module are My account, Help (the start of this manual) and Log out.

A red number at a menu item tells how many new records you have not seen yet are on the page - for example new inquiries, job applications, orders, products below the stock limit, leads overdue for contact or security events. The number is personal: it counts from your last visit of the page and disappears once you open it. Above 99 records it shows “99+”. The module switcher shows the sum of unread records of all modules (in its list every module has its own number) and a collapsed menu section its sum too; on a phone a dot on the menu button tells you. The system asks for news once a minute, and only while the admin tab is open in the foreground. When a number grows, a notice appears at the top right - click it to open the page. You see numbers only at pages you have permission for. An orange dot means work waiting for you - for example website or e-shop texts and website content (FAQ, jobs, references, knowledge base) missing a translation in an active language (typically after an update of the application). The dot is at the page, the menu section, the module in the switcher and on the switcher itself - also next to a red number, so it does not get lost. Opening the page does not clear it, filling the texts does. Hover over a number or a dot to see what exactly it counts - for example “Missing website texts: 123 (English 120, Czech 3)”.

The menu opens with the button at the top left and closes with a tap outside it. The module switcher is in the middle of the header. Your profile photo at the top right opens the account panel: e-mail and role, My account, calendar, administration language and Log out. My account and Help are also at the bottom of the menu.

sections.heading: 04. Switching between Core and the applications

items: Click the Core tab in the header to work with the system pages (accounts, settings, legal documents, logs).
Click the Applications button and choose an application to work with the website, the e-shop or the project portal.
The left menu switches to the pages of the chosen module and its first page you may open is shown (usually the welcome page or the dashboard).

blocks.content: An application you have no permission for is not offered at all. The overview of all applications with their state (online, maintenance, problem) is on the Applications page.

items: The question mark in the header of every page opens the chapter of the manual about that page.
Help at the bottom of the left menu opens the start of the manual.
In the manual, choose a chapter on the left. Chapters are grouped: general chapters, Core and the individual applications.
At the top right of the manual you switch its language; at the top left the Administration button takes you back to the administration.
On a phone the list of chapters opens with the menu button of the manual.

blocks.content: At the end of every chapter is the contact of the system's author for reporting an error in the system or in the manual.

sections.heading: 06. Tables - the basis of most pages

blocks.content: Most pages that manage records (accounts, inquiries, orders, products, logs …) use the same table. It works the same everywhere:

cards.title: Actions menu
cards.text: Drop-down button above the table. Depending on the page and your permissions it offers: open and hide filters, add a record, export data, import data, charts and reports, and switching between active records and the trash.

cards.title: Table row
cards.text: One row = one record. Long texts are shortened; the full content is in the record details.

cards.title: Icons at the end of a row
cards.text: Actions with one record: magnifier or Details (show all data), pencil or Edit (edit) and bin or Delete (move to the trash). Some pages have more actions, described in their chapter. You do not see icons you have no permission for.

cards.title: Checkboxes
cards.text: On pages that allow it, each row starts with a checkbox. The checkbox in the header selects all records on the current page of the table.

cards.title: Pagination
cards.text: Below the table: the information “Showing 1 - 10 of 57 records”, page buttons and the number of items per page. An empty table shows no pagination - the table itself tells that it has no records.

cards.title: Freshness of the data
cards.text: The table shows the time of the last update and a button to load the current data at once. The data also refreshes by itself about every 15 minutes while the browser tab is open and active.

cards.title: Table width
cards.text: The option Show table at full page width stretches the table over the whole width - useful for tables with many columns.

cards.title: Empty table
cards.text: The message “No data found.” means that no record matches the filters, or that there are no records yet.

items: Tick the checkboxes of the records you want to work with (or the checkbox in the header for the whole page).
A bar with the number of selected records appears above the table.
The Actions button in the bar offers Export selected and - when the page allows it and you may delete - Delete selected.
Confirm a bulk deletion in the dialog. The records move to the trash; afterwards the dialog tells you how many were deleted and how many could not be.
The Clear selection button unticks all records.

blocks.content: On some pages bulk deletion is switched off on purpose (for example administrator accounts) - records are deleted one by one there.

steps.label: Open the filters
steps.text: In the Actions menu choose to open the filters. The filter panel slides out on the right.

steps.label: Search across all columns
steps.text: Type any term into the top field - the table shows records that contain it in any column.

steps.label: Column filters
steps.text: Below are fields for individual columns (text, choice from a list, date …). You can fill in several at once - a record must match all of them.

steps.label: Sorting
steps.text: In Sort by choose a column and in Sort direction choose ascending (A-Z, smallest first) or descending (Z-A, largest first).

steps.label: Apply filters
steps.text: The Apply filters button filters the table and takes you to the first page of the results.

steps.label: Clear filters
steps.text: The Clear filters button empties all fields and shows all records again.

blocks.content: Close the panel with the cross or the hide-filters item in the Actions menu. The filters stay applied until you clear them.

sections.heading: 09. Forms - adding and editing a record

items: Add a new record with the create item in the Actions menu, edit an existing one with the edit icon in its row.
A form opens. Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required.
A wrongly filled field is highlighted when you leave it and the reason is shown below it (for example “This field is required.” or “Invalid email format.”).
Choice fields offer only allowed values. Fields with several options are ticked; options taken over from a role are marked and cannot be unticked.

For attachments choose files with the button or drag them into the marked area. Below the field you see the allowed number of files, the maximum size and the allowed types; a file that breaks a limit is refused with an explanation.
Confirm saves the form, Cancel or the cross closes it without saving.

blocks.content: If the message Invalid form appears after Confirm, a required field is missing or wrongly filled. The form stays open and nothing was saved - correct the highlighted fields and confirm again.

The details icon (magnifier, Details) opens a window with all data of the record, including what does not fit into the table, and the dates of creation and last change. The details only show - nothing can be changed there. Attachments have the buttons View (opens the file in the browser) and Download.
Deleting a record has two steps so that nothing is lost by mistake:

steps.label: Delete
steps.text: The bin icon in a row (after confirmation) moves the record to the trash. It disappears from the table, but nothing is lost.

steps.label: Trash
steps.text: In the Actions menu choose Show trash. You see the deleted records with the date of deletion. Show active takes you back to the active records.

steps.label: Restore
steps.text: The Restore button returns the record to the active ones with all its data.

steps.label: Delete permanently
steps.text: Removes one record for good. This step cannot be undone.

steps.label: Empty trash
steps.text: Permanently deletes all records in the trash. Records that other data depending on them must keep (for example a customer with orders) are not deleted and the dialog says so.

blocks.content: Permanent deletion and emptying the trash cannot be undone. Before you confirm, make sure you really do not need the records.

You only see the trash with the permission to show deleted records in the trash (view-deleted). Restoring and permanent deletion also need the delete permission of the page. Old records in the trash may also be deleted automatically by the nightly clean-up according to the retention settings (Legal documents → Data retention).

items: In the Actions menu choose to export data (or Export selected in the bulk actions bar - then only the ticked records are exported).
Choose the format: CSV (Excel, Google Sheets), XLSX (Excel workbook), JSON (for developers and integrations) or TXT (plain text with tabs).
Tick the columns the file should contain (Select all / Deselect all). At least one column must be selected.
The option Export in raw format uses technical column names and unformatted values - such a file can be imported straight back (into this or another instance of the system).
Confirm. The system prepares the file and the browser downloads it.

blocks.content: Exported files often contain personal data (names, e-mails, phone numbers). Keep them only where they are protected, do not send them unprotected and delete them after use. Every export is written to the log.

In a CSV and TXT export, a value a spreadsheet (Excel, LibreOffice) would run as a formula - it starts with =, +, -, @ - gets an apostrophe in front, so it is shown as plain text. This protects against formulas slipped in through the public forms. The import removes the apostrophe again; numbers (for example -5) stay unchanged.

Some pages (for example the inquiries of the website, the leads of the project portal or the suppliers of the e-shop) have an import item in the Actions menu. Import only bulk-adds new records - it never overwrites or deletes existing data.

steps.label: Download the template
steps.text: The Download blank template button downloads a file with the correct column headers. For columns with a fixed set of values the window shows the allowed values.

steps.label: Fill in the file
steps.text: Every row = one new record. Do not change the column headers.

steps.label: Upload and check
steps.text: Choose the file and press Check file. Nothing is saved yet - you see the number of total, valid and invalid rows and the exact reason for every invalid row.

steps.label: Confirm
steps.text: The Confirm and add N records button adds only the valid rows. Rows that collide with an existing record are skipped.

steps.label: Result
steps.text: The window shows how many records were added and how many skipped. A large import runs in the background - its result is then in the log of the application.

blocks.content: If no row is valid, the import cannot be confirmed - fix the file according to the listed errors and upload it again. The Back button returns you to the file choice.

items: In the Actions menu choose to generate charts and reports. A window with the report settings panel opens.
In Period fill in the From and To dates. An empty field means no limit.

In Columns and chart type tick the columns to evaluate and choose a chart type for each - bar, pie, doughnut, radar, polar or trend over time. For numeric values you choose a line or bar chart and the sum or average.
The Values button of a column lets you choose which values the chart includes (the others are left out and the report says so).
The option Overall trend over time adds a chart of the total number of records over time.
Press Generate report. The step of the chart (day, week, month) follows the length of the period.
Export to PDF saves the report as a document with its date, period and number of records.

blocks.highlight: Why a chart does not show zero values
blocks.content: Pie and doughnut charts cannot show values with a zero count. When you need to see them, choose radar, polar or trend over time.

cards.title: Confirmation dialog
cards.text: Before every action that deletes or changes a lot, the system asks. Confirm performs the action, Cancel cancels it.

cards.title: Result messages
cards.text: After saving or deleting a short confirmation appears. An error message always says what failed - nothing was saved in that case.

cards.title: Password confirmation
cards.text: Sensitive operations (switching an application off and on, operations with system administrator accounts, the allowed e-mail domains, changing your own login e-mail) are carried out only after you enter your current password. After a correct password the system does not ask again for the same operation for 10 minutes.

cards.title: Connection error
cards.text: A message that the server cannot be reached means an internet or server outage. Check the connection and repeat the action.

sections.heading: 16. The pages “Page not found” and “Access denied”

items: Page not found: there is nothing at the address in the administration - the address is wrong or the page was moved. Continue from the menu.
Access denied: the page exists, but your account has no permission to open it. If you need it, ask the accounts administrator for the permission.
Both pages show the requested address and offer the buttons Back and Administration home.

blocks.content: After an update of the system a bar “Updated to … - N change(s) here” briefly appears above the page. It is shown only in the part you work in and only when the update changed it. What's new opens the list of changes, the cross hides the bar until the next update. All versions and changes are on the Releases page.

items: Never lend your account or tell anybody your password - every person should have an account of their own.
On a shared or foreign computer always log out with Log out and do not use Remember me.
Every change in the administration (creating, editing, deleting, exporting, signing in) is written to the log with your account, the time and the IP address.
Work with the personal data of customers, clients and applicants only as far as your work requires (GDPR).
When you do not know what to do, open the question mark of the page. If you still do not know, use the contacts in the chapter Contacts and help.

security.header: Signing in, passwords and account security

blocks.content: This chapter explains everything about access to the administration: signing in, saved accounts, two-factor authentication, password rules, a forgotten password, how long a sign-in lasts, logging out and how the system protects accounts against misuse.

steps.label: Open the sign-in page
steps.text: The address of the administration takes you to the sign-in. The logo is on the left, the sign-in card on the right, the language choice at the top right.

steps.label: E-mail and password
steps.text: Enter your login e-mail and password. The eye icon shows the password so you can check it.

steps.label: Remember me
steps.text: Tick it only on your own computer - see chapter 03.

steps.label: Sign in
steps.text: Press Sign in. Without two-factor authentication you are signed in.

steps.label: Verification code
steps.text: With two-factor authentication a six-digit code arrives at your e-mail. Enter it and press Verify.

blocks.content: With a wrong e-mail or password the system does not reveal, for security reasons, what exactly was wrong. Check both and try again.

items: After three failed sign-ins to one e-mail within 15 minutes the system also requires a check that you are not a robot (CAPTCHA). Confirm it and sign in again.
The number of attempts per minute is limited (per e-mail and per network). When you exceed it, wait a minute.
Every failed attempt and every suspicious behaviour is written to the security monitoring, where the system administrator sees it.

blocks.content: The option Remember me decides how long a sign-in lasts:

cards.title: Without remembering
cards.text: The sign-in ends when the browser is closed, at the latest after 12 hours of inactivity.

cards.title: With remembering
cards.text: The sign-in survives closing the browser. It ends after 7 days in which you do not use the administration at all.

cards.title: Always at most 30 days
cards.text: At the latest 30 days after signing in you must sign in again - including two-factor authentication - even if you use the administration every day.

blocks.content: On the sign-in page remembered accounts are offered under Continue with a saved account - one click on Continue as … signs you in without a password. The account of the current window is marked Signed in in this window. If an account meanwhile stopped existing or being valid, the system says it is no longer available and you have to sign in with the password.
One browser can have several accounts signed in - every tab works with one of them. Signing in or choosing an account affects only the current tab; the other tabs keep their account.
Never tick Remember me on a shared, public or foreign computer.
Two-factor authentication means a password is not enough to sign in - you also need a code sent to your e-mail. Someone who knows only your password cannot sign in.

items: The code has 6 digits and is valid for 10 minutes; the sign-in page shows how long it remains valid.
You can enter the code at most five times. After that you must sign in again with your password.
Resend code requests a new code - at the earliest after 60 seconds and at most five times per sign-in. A new code cancels the previous one.
When the code does not arrive, check the spam folder and that the e-mail of your account is correct.

cards.title: Turning on and off
cards.text: On the My account page (Security tab) you turn 2FA on or off yourself with the checkbox Two-factor authentication (2FA).

cards.title: Mandatory for a role
cards.text: Some roles always require 2FA (the sysadmin role always, others according to the role settings). The checkbox then cannot be turned off.

cards.title: Enforced by an administrator
cards.text: The system administrator can enforce 2FA for a specific account. It then cannot be turned off either - contact the administrator.

blocks.content: We recommend keeping 2FA always on, especially if you have access to personal data or to account management.
The same rules apply to account activation, resetting a forgotten password and changing a password:

items: 8 to 64 characters,
at least one letter,
at least one digit,
at least one special character (for example ! ? # % - _ .).

blocks.content: While you type a new password, the list of requirements is shown below the field and the met ones are highlighted. The confirmation must match the password.

blocks.highlight: How to choose a good password
blocks.content: Safest is a long phrase of several words with a digit and a symbol, or a password generated by a password manager. Do not reuse a password from elsewhere and do not use your name, date of birth or the company name.

steps.label: Forgot password?
steps.text: On the sign-in page click the link Forgot password?

steps.label: Enter the e-mail
steps.text: Type your login e-mail and press Send reset link.

steps.label: Check your mail
steps.text: The system always answers “If the account exists, a reset link is on its way.” - for security reasons it does not reveal whether the account exists. The link is valid for 60 minutes.

steps.label: New password
steps.text: The link opens the page Set a new password. Enter a password according to the rules, repeat it and press Set new password.

steps.label: Sign in
steps.text: After a successful change the page takes you to the sign-in.

blocks.content: The link can be used once. If it expired or was used, the page says it is invalid - request a new one on the sign-in page. A new request can be sent after a minute at the earliest.

sections.heading: 07. Changing the password and the login e-mail

items: Change your password on the My account page (Security tab) with Change password: enter the current password, the new password and its confirmation.
After a password change all other sign-ins of your account end (other browsers, other devices, other tabs) - the current tab stays signed in.

The login e-mail is changed by the accounts administrator. If you change it yourself (only with the permission), the system first checks your password, ends the other sign-ins and sends a notice to the old and the new address.
If you receive a notice of a change you did not make, contact the administrator immediately.

blocks.content: The Log out button is at the very bottom of the left menu. It logs out the account of the current tab - on the server and in the browser. Other tabs with the same account go to the sign-in page; other accounts signed in in this browser stay signed in. When a sign-in expires, the system takes you to the sign-in page by itself and you sign in again.

items: An account that has not been activated yet (has no password) cannot sign in. Use the activation link from the e-mail or ask the administrator for a new one.
A blocked account cannot sign in and its running sign-ins are ended. Only the system administrator can block and unblock an account.
In both cases the sign-in page says that signing in to this account is not allowed and recommends contacting the administrator.

cards.title: Encrypted connection
cards.text: The administration talks to the server only encrypted (HTTPS).

cards.title: Passwords
cards.text: A password is never stored in readable form - not even the system administrator can find it out, only send a link to set a new one.

cards.title: Stolen sign-in
cards.text: When the system finds that the same sign-in is used from two different places, it ends all sign-ins of the account and records a security event.

cards.title: Security monitoring
cards.text: Failed sign-ins, wrong codes, robots and scans are written to the security monitoring checked by the administrator.

cards.title: Audit
cards.text: Sign-ins, logouts, password changes and all data changes are written to the logs.

cards.title: Password confirmation
cards.text: The most sensitive operations require your password again even while you are signed in.

cards.title: The activation e-mail did not arrive
cards.text: Check the spam folder. The activation link is valid for 48 hours; then ask the administrator to resend it.

cards.title: The verification code did not arrive
cards.text: Wait a minute, check the spam folder and use Resend code.

cards.title: The code expired
cards.text: Request a new code with Resend code, or sign in again.

cards.title: The system logged me out
cards.text: The sign-in expired or was ended (password change, blocking, suspected stolen sign-in). Sign in again.

cards.title: I suspect misuse of my account
cards.text: Change your password immediately, turn on 2FA and tell the administrator - they will check the security monitoring.

contacts.header: Contacts and where to get help

blocks.content: Whom to contact when you do not know what to do, something does not work or you need to change your access.

sections.heading: 01. What to do when you are stuck

items: Open the question mark in the header of the page you work with - the chapter of the manual describes every function of the page and has a part What to do when …
Read the introductory chapter How to work with the administration - it explains tables, filters, forms, the trash, export and import, which are the same on all pages.
If the problem persists, contact your administrator (chapter 02).
Report an error of the system to its author (chapter 03).

blocks.content: The accounts administrator is a person in your company who has access to the Accounts page and manages users. Contact them when:

items: you need a new account for a colleague or to close the account of a leaving employee,
a page, button or application is missing (extended permissions or another role),
your activation e-mail did not arrive or expired,
your name or login e-mail needs to change,
your account is blocked or you suspect it was misused.

blocks.content: Only the system administrator (the sysadmin role) may change roles and the allowed e-mail domains, block accounts and enforce two-factor authentication.

sections.heading: 03. The author of the system and technical support

blocks.content: The system was created and is technically maintained by JonclSolutions. The contact is also at the end of every chapter of this manual.
When reporting an error give as many details as possible - it speeds up the fix:

items: the address of the page (from the address bar of the browser),
what you did and what you expected,
the exact wording of the error message (ideally a screenshot),
the date and approximate time of the error,
the browser and device (for example Chrome on Windows, Safari on an iPhone).

blocks.content: Never put passwords, verification codes or personal data of customers into a report. Nobody from support will ever ask you for your password or code.
The contact e-mail, phone, address and social media that visitors of the website, the e-shop and the client portal see are set in Core on the Company profile page (tab Company details).

The system dashboard is a quick overview of the shared resources Core manages for all applications: user accounts, roles, legal documents, external links and system logs. From here one click takes you to every management page of Core.
Only accounts with the permission for the Core section (view-core) see the dashboard. Each tile and card is shown only with the permission for its page - so everyone may see a different dashboard.
The header shows the title System overview, the time of the last update and the Refresh button. The data loads when the page opens; the button loads it again at any time.

cards.title: Main tile
cards.text: The big number at the top left. Click its name to open a menu and choose which metric is highlighted: System users, Roles & permissions, Legal documents, External links or System logs.

cards.title: Overview by module
cards.text: Bar overview of the other metrics - for a quick comparison of sizes.

cards.title: Distribution
cards.text: A coloured bar showing the proportion of the metrics to each other. It is shown only when at least two metrics are available.

cards.title: No overviews
cards.text: The message “No overview data is available for your account.” means you have no permission for any of the measured pages.

items: System users - the number of user accounts of the administration (page Accounts).
Roles & permissions - the number of roles (system administrators only).
Legal documents - the number of sections of the legal documents.
External links - the number of your external links.
System logs - the number of entries in the system log.

blocks.content: Cards with the name and description of a page - Accounts, Roles & permissions, Legal documents, External links, System logs and Company profile. Click a card to open it. Cards of pages you have no permission for are not shown.

A list of the last eight entries of the system log (sign-ins, logouts, changes of accounts, roles and documents, password reset requests …) with the time and the user. View all opens the System logs page with the full history and filters. The card Recent events breakdown shows how many of these entries were creations, updates, deletions, restorations, exports and errors.
You see at a glance whether anything unusual is happening - for example a series of failed sign-ins or unexpected deletions. Look for the details in System logs and in Security monitoring.

The calendar gathers in one place the important dates of all modules (start and end of discount coupons, project deadlines, lead follow-ups, expiring links) and the open work (new inquiries, new applications, orders to process …). You can also add your own personal reminders.
Every signed-in user sees the calendar. The dates and tasks of the modules are shown only from pages you have permission for. Only you see your personal events.

items: in the account panel - click your e-mail in the header (on a phone the profile photo at the top right),
with the Calendar item in the Core menu, section Overview.

blocks.content: Above the calendar is a panel with work that is waiting for someone. Each item shows the count and the age of the oldest waiting record (for example “oldest 3 days ago”). Click an item to open the page where you handle the work. When nothing waits, the panel shows All done.

cards.title: System
cards.text: New security events nobody has evaluated yet.

cards.title: Web
cards.text: New inquiries from the website and new job applications.

cards.title: E-shop
cards.text: E-shop orders to process and products with low stock.

cards.title: Project portal
cards.text: Leads without contact for 14 days or more and orders without a project yet.

cards.title: Activation expires
cards.text: The day the activation link of a new account stops working (System).

cards.title: Coupon starts / ends

cards.title: Follow up

cards.title: Form expires
