cards.title: Personal events
cards.text: Your own reminders (chapter 05).

blocks.content: The dates of the modules come automatically from the data of the administration - you do not create or edit them in the calendar. Click a date to open the page it belongs to. A date that has passed without being handled is marked Overdue.

cards.title: Month / List
cards.text: View switch: a month grid, or a clear list of the dates of the month.

cards.title: Arrows and Today
cards.text: The arrows go to the previous or next month, Today returns to the current month.

cards.title: Shown modules
cards.text: Coloured switches of the modules (System, Personal, Web, E-shop, Project portal). Switching a module off hides its dates. Every module has its own colour in the calendar.

cards.title: A full day
cards.text: When not all dates fit into a day, “+N more” is shown. All dates of the day are in the List view.

steps.label: Add event
steps.text: The Add event button (or adding directly on a day) opens the form New personal event.

steps.label: Title
steps.text: A required short description, for example “Call the supplier”.

steps.label: Date and time
steps.text: The date is required. The time is optional - an empty time means all day.

steps.label: Note
steps.text: Optional longer text.

steps.label: Done
steps.text: Ticking it marks the event as handled.

steps.label: Save
steps.text: The event appears in the calendar in the Personal colour.

items: Click your event to edit it (form Edit personal event).
Mark as done / Mark as not done change the state without opening the form.
Delete removes the event permanently after confirmation - it cannot be undone.

blocks.content: Only you see your personal events - not even administrators see them. Still, do not write sensitive personal data of customers into them.

cards.title: The calendar did not load
cards.text: The message “The calendar could not be loaded” is shown. Reload the page; if it persists, contact support.

cards.title: Dates of a module are missing
cards.text: You have no permission for the page the dates come from, or the module is switched off in Shown modules.

cards.title: A date is wrong
cards.text: Correct the data on the page the date comes from (coupon, project, lead) - the calendar follows by itself.

blocks.content: The welcome page opens right after signing in. It greets you by name and shows the basic details of your account. It contains no sensitive overviews - those are on the dashboards.

cards.title: Greeting
cards.text: The heading “Welcome to the administration, …” with your name.

cards.title: Your profile
cards.text: Full name, login e-mail, role and the date the account was created.

cards.title: Help
cards.text: A pointer to technical support and the system administrator at the bottom of the page.

blocks.content: If the profile cannot be loaded, the message “Failed to load your profile.” is shown - reload the page. Change your details on the My account page (at the bottom of the menu or in the account panel - click your e-mail in the header).

The page requires the permission to show the welcome page (core-view-welcome-page). It is recommended for every account - without it the user sees the Access denied page after signing in and has to continue from the menu.

items: The left menu - pages of the Core module.
The module switcher in the header - website, e-shop, project portal.
The calendar in the account panel (click your e-mail in the header) - dates and open work.
Help at the bottom of the left menu - this manual.

edit-legal.header: Legal documents - privacy policy, terms of service, cookies, data retention

blocks.content: On this page you edit the texts of the legal documents visitors see on the website and in the e-shop: the privacy policy (GDPR), the terms of service (TOS) and the cookies policy. Each document consists of sections and exists separately in every language of the website.
Legal documents have legal force. Consult changes with a lawyer and after editing check that the text is the same in all languages.

cards.title: Privacy policy (GDPR)
cards.text: Website: /privacy-policy, e-shop: /shop/privacy-policy. Forms in which a visitor gives consent link to it too.

cards.title: Terms of service (TOS)
cards.text: Website: /tos, e-shop: /shop/tos.

cards.title: Cookies
cards.text: Website: /cookies-policy. The page also has a button to change the cookie settings.

blocks.content: The documents are shared by all applications: a text edited once is shown on the website and in the e-shop (each in its own look). The date of the last update below the document follows the last edit automatically.

sections.heading: 02. Finding your way on the page

cards.title: Document tabs
cards.text: At the top you choose the document: GDPR, TOS, Cookies. The last tab Data retention sets how long personal data are kept (chapter 08).

cards.title: Language tabs
cards.text: Below them you choose the language. The languages are the languages of all applications together. A language in which some sections are missing has a warning mark.

cards.title: Number of missing translations
cards.text: The mark next to the title shows how many translations are missing across all languages.

cards.title: List of sections
cards.text: The sections of the current document in the current language in the order the visitor sees them. Each has a heading and content.

blocks.content: Every section has a position (order number). Sections with the same position in different languages are translations of the same section. When a section at some position is missing in a language, the system reports it:

items: a bar above the sections: “In language … N sections missing that exist in other languages”, with Fill position N buttons,
a mark “missing in N lang.” at a section of another language - hover over it to see in which languages.

blocks.content: When a document has no section in the visitor's language, the Czech version is shown; when it has no Czech one either, an existing language is shown. A new installation has English templates with details in square brackets (for example [Company name], [Contact e-mail]) - these must be replaced with real details.

steps.label: Choose the document and language
steps.text: Click the tab of the document and of the language.

steps.label: Edit
steps.text: Press Edit at the section. It switches to editing.

steps.label: Section heading
steps.text: An optional heading, for example “1. Introductory provisions”.

steps.label: Section content
steps.text: The required text of the section. Empty content cannot be saved.

steps.label: Save
steps.text: Save confirms the change, Cancel discards it. The change shows on the public website at once.

blocks.content: The content of a section is one paragraph. For another paragraph create a new section (without a heading if you do not need one). Line breaks inside the content are not shown on the website.

items: Below the list of sections press Add section - the new section is added at the end of the document in the current language.
To fill in a missing translation, use the Fill position N button in the bar of missing sections - the section is created right at that position.
Fill in the heading and the content (both are required when adding) and press Save.

blocks.content: After you add a section in one language the system at once shows it is missing in the other languages. Add it in all languages so that the document says the same everywhere.

The bin icon at a section and a confirmation in the dialog delete the section. Deletion cannot be undone and affects only the section in the current language - the translations in other languages stay and the system then marks them as missing elsewhere.

cards.title: Viewing
cards.text: Show legal documents (core-legal-documents-view).

cards.title: Adding a section
cards.text: Create a new section of a legal document (core-legal-documents-create).

cards.title: Editing a section
cards.text: Edit a section of a legal document (core-legal-documents-update).

cards.title: Deleting a section
cards.text: Delete a section of a legal document (core-legal-documents-delete).

cards.title: Data retention
cards.text: View company details (core-legal-config-view); saving the periods and the clean-up need edit company details (core-legal-config-update).

blocks.content: Buttons you have no permission for are not shown. Every change is written to the system log.

The Data retention tab is the last one in the row of documents. Accounts with the permission to view company details (core-legal-config-view) see it; only the permission to edit company details (core-legal-config-update) saves the periods and runs the clean-up. An account allowed only the retention and not the documents sees it right after opening the page.

The GDPR requires that personal data is not kept longer than necessary. On this tab you set for every kind of data after how long it is deleted automatically. The clean-up runs every night and permanently deletes records that have not changed for longer than the set period - including their attachments, files and items in the trash. Records being worked on (changed recently) are therefore not deleted.

cards.title: Cookie consent records
cards.text: An anonymous proof of the visitor's consent (without the IP address). Usually 3 years.

cards.title: Audit logs (core, web, e-shop)
cards.text: History of changes with the e-mail and IP address of who made them, and the history of imports. Usually 1-2 years.

cards.title: Web inquiries
cards.text: Pre-contract communication. Usually 1-2 years.

cards.title: Job applications (CV)
cards.text: Without the applicant's consent to a longer record usually 6 months.

cards.title: Leads
cards.text: Business opportunities and their contacts. Usually 1-2 years.

cards.title: Orders (project portal)
cards.text: A contractual relationship - accounting and tax rules may require up to 10 years.

cards.title: Projects (client portal)
cards.text: Including threads, messages and attachments; the last message in the portal counts as well.

blocks.content: Rows of applications are shown only for installed applications. For every row choose a period (30 days to 10 years) or Do not delete automatically. Below the card you see when the last clean-up ran and how many records it deleted.

items: Set the periods and press Save periods.
The clean-up runs at night by itself. To run it at once, press Run clean-up now and confirm - records older than the SAVED periods are deleted.

blocks.content: The clean-up deletes permanently and cannot be undone. Before shortening a period make sure you really do not need the older data (for example for complaints, accounting or disputes).

E-shop orders and customers are not deleted automatically - they are subject to accounting periods. Expired sign-ins to the client portal are always deleted. Security monitoring has its own retention on its page.

The page of your own account. It has three tabs: Profile (profile photo and your details), Security (two-factor authentication and the password change) and Preferences (administration language and pop-up notices). Every signed-in user can open it.

Open it with the My account item at the bottom of the menu (in every module) or in the account panel - click your e-mail in the header (on a phone the profile photo at the top right). The open tab is in the address of the page, so you can bookmark it.

items: Click Change photo and choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image of at most 2 MB.
The photo uploads at once (“Uploading the photo…” is shown) and appears in the admin header and at your account in the list of accounts.
Remove photo deletes it and the default image is shown.

blocks.content: On an error the reason is shown: a format other than JPG, PNG and WebP, or a photo larger than 2 MB.

cards.title: Full name
cards.text: The name shown in the administration and in the greeting of e-mails.

cards.title: Login e-mail
cards.text: The address you sign in with and where verification codes and notices go.

cards.title: Role
cards.text: Your role - it decides what you may do in the administration. The accounts administrator changes it.

blocks.content: A regular user does not change the name or the e-mail - the page title has a note to contact an administrator. The system administrator and a user with the permission to edit accounts (core-administrators-update) see the buttons Change name and Change login e-mail.

sections.heading: 03. Changing the name and e-mail (with the permission only)

steps.label: Change
steps.text: Click Change name or Change login e-mail. The value turns into an input field.

steps.label: New value
steps.text: The name may have at most 255 characters, the e-mail must be valid.

steps.label: Save
steps.text: Save confirms, Cancel returns the original value.

steps.label: Password (e-mail only)
steps.text: Before changing the e-mail the system asks for your current password.

steps.label: After changing the e-mail
steps.text: The other sign-ins of your account end and the old and the new address receive a notice. The new e-mail shows in the header at once; next time you sign in with the new e-mail.

blocks.content: The Security tab has the checkbox Two-factor authentication (2FA). The change is saved right after the click and applies from the next sign-in. The text below the checkbox always says the state of the authentication:

cards.title: Disabled
cards.text: “Two-factor authentication is disabled.” We recommend turning it on.

cards.title: Enabled
cards.text: “Two-factor authentication is enabled.” You can turn it off at any time.

cards.title: Mandatory for the role
cards.text: Your role requires the authentication - the checkbox is locked.

cards.title: Enforced by an administrator
cards.text: The system administrator enforced the authentication for your account - the checkbox is locked; contact the administrator.

blocks.content: How the authentication works at sign-in is described in the chapter Access and security.

steps.label: Change password
steps.text: On the Security tab press Change password. The Change password window opens.

steps.label: Current password
steps.text: Enter your current password.

steps.label: New password and confirmation
steps.text: Enter the new password (8 to 64 characters, a letter, a digit and a special character) and repeat it. Below the field you see which requirements the password already meets; a mismatching confirmation is marked at once.

steps.label: Update password
steps.text: After saving a confirmation is shown. All other sign-ins of your account (other browsers, devices and tabs) end, the current tab stays signed in.

blocks.content: The message “Error changing password. Please check your current password.” means the current password does not match or the new password breaks the rules. The password was not changed.
Reset a forgotten password on the sign-in page with the link Forgot password? (chapter Access and security).
On the Preferences tab choose the language of the administration (Czech or English). The change applies at once, without saving. The same choice is in the account panel.

items: The choice applies only in this browser - set it separately in another browser or on another device.
The language is also used on the sign-in page.

blocks.content: The Preferences tab has the checkbox Show pop-up notices of new records. When it is on, a notice appears at the top right every time a new record arrives (for example an inquiry or an order); click the notice to open its page.

items: The choice applies only in this browser - set it separately in another browser or on another device.
The red numbers of unread records and the orange dots of work waiting for you are always shown in the menu, even when the notices are off.
A notice holds only the number and the kind of records, never names or e-mails.

settings.header: Company profile - company details and page titles

blocks.content: The Company profile page has two tabs: Company details (logo, company details and social media shown to visitors and in e-mails) and Page titles (the name of the administration in the browser tab). How long personal data are kept is set on the Legal documents page, tab Data retention.

Accounts with the permission to show company details (core-legal-config-view) see the page. Only accounts with the permission to edit company details (core-legal-config-update) may save; adding and deleting social media have permissions of their own.

steps.label: Choose logo
steps.text: In the Logo card press Choose logo (or Change logo). Choose a JPG, PNG or SVG image up to 2 MB.

steps.label: Preview
steps.text: The logo appears in the preview with the mark New logo ready to save. Cancel selection discards it.

steps.label: Saving
steps.text: The logo is saved only with the Save company details button at the bottom (the button shows “+ logo”).

blocks.content: The logo is shown in the header of the public website and the e-shop and as the icon in the tab preview on the Page titles tabs.

cards.title: Company name *
cards.text: Required. Shown on the website, in the e-shop and in e-mails.

cards.title: Contact e-mail *
cards.text: Required. The contact for visitors - website, e-shop, maintenance pages, e-mails.

cards.title: Brand tagline
cards.text: The company slogan - entered separately for every language.

cards.title: Copyright text
cards.text: The copyright notice - separately for every language.

cards.title: Company ID and VAT ID
cards.text: The registration and tax numbers of the company.

cards.title: Phone and Address
cards.text: The contact phone and the address of the registered office or premises.

cards.title: Website footer text
cards.text: Text in the footer of the public website, for example “© 2026 Company Ltd. All rights reserved.”

cards.title: Google Analytics 4 - Measurement ID
cards.text: The Google Analytics measurement ID (starts with G-). Measuring starts on the website only for a visitor who agrees to analytics cookies. Empty field = no measuring.

blocks.content: For the language fields (tagline, copyright) switch the language with the switch Language for tagline and copyright above the form. Fill them in for all languages.

Apart from the required fields, every detail has the checkbox Show on the website next to its name. A switched-off detail is not shown on the website or in e-mails, but its value stays saved. A switched-on detail must be filled in - otherwise saving ends with the message Missing details and a list of the fields.
Save everything with Save company details. A successful save is confirmed by the message and the Saved mark at the card.

steps.label: Add social media
steps.text: Add social media creates a new row.

steps.label: Name and address
steps.text: Fill in the name (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn …) and the full address of the profile starting with https://.

steps.label: Icon
steps.text: Upload icon chooses the icon image (up to 2 MB) - it is shown on the website at the link.

steps.label: Save
steps.text: The save icon of the row saves the link. Every row is saved on its own.

steps.label: Delete
steps.text: The bin icon and a confirmation delete the link together with its icon.

blocks.content: Social media are shown on the public website, in the e-shop, in the client portal and on the maintenance pages. Adding requires core-legal-config-create, editing core-legal-config-update and deleting core-legal-config-delete.
Here you set the text shown in the browser tab for the whole administration and the sign-in pages (row Whole administration and login), separately for every language of the administration.

items: Choose the language with the switch Language of the titles.
Edit the title in the field. The tab preview above the field shows how the tab will look.
Save page titles saves the changes; Discard changes reverts them. The number of unsaved changes is above the buttons.

blocks.content: Empty field = the Czech title is used. The recommended length is up to 60 characters. Page titles of the website and the e-shop are set in their applications (Edit website, Edit e-shop).

external-links.header: External links - your bookmarks of tools

blocks.content: External links are your personal bookmarks of tools outside the administration - for example Google Analytics, Search Console, webmail, accounting or the domain management. You have them at hand in one place in the administration.
The links are private: every user sees and manages only their own links. Colleagues do not see yours and you do not see theirs.

The table has the columns ID, Name and URL. It works like the other tables of the administration (Actions menu, filters, pagination, export, charts and the trash - see the introductory chapter). Copy the address of a link from the table or from the details (magnifier icon) and open it in a new browser tab.

steps.label: Add record
steps.text: In the Actions menu choose Add record.

steps.label: Link name
steps.text: A short name, for example “Google Analytics”. Required, at most 150 characters.

steps.label: URL address
steps.text: The full address starting with http:// or https://.

steps.label: Confirm
steps.text: The link is saved and appears in the table.

items: The edit icon in a row opens the form with the data of the link; Confirm saves the changes.
The bin icon moves the link to the trash. In the trash you restore it or delete it permanently.

cards.title: Viewing
cards.text: core-external-links-view

cards.title: Adding
cards.text: core-external-links-create

cards.title: Editing
cards.text: core-external-links-update

cards.title: Deleting and restoring from the trash
cards.text: core-external-links-delete; the trash also requires the permission to show deleted records (view-deleted).

blocks.content: Do not store user names, passwords or addresses with secret tokens in the links. Store only the normal address of the tool's page.

A role is a named set of permissions, for example “Sales” or “Content manager”. Every account has one role and it decides which pages the account may open and which actions it may take. On this page you create, edit and delete roles and decide which permissions they contain.
The page is available only to the system administrator (the sysadmin role). A change of a role applies at once to all accounts that have it - make it with care.

sections.heading: 01. Finding your way on the page

cards.title: Role list (left)
cards.text: All roles with the search field Search role…. Each role shows the number of accounts that have it, a 2FA icon (the role requires two-factor authentication) and the System role mark.

cards.title: Role detail (right)
cards.text: Name, description, the 2FA setting and the list of permissions of the selected role. Until you select a role it shows Select a role from the list on the left, or create a new one.

cards.title: Buttons New role and Export
cards.text: At the right of the detail header.

blocks.content: Permissions are grouped by module (System (Core), Web, E-shop, Project portal …) and inside a module by page. Each has an understandable description and a technical key. The key is made of the module, the page and the action, for example:

cards.title: …-view
cards.text: Show the page and its data.

cards.title: …-create
cards.text: Add records.

cards.title: …-update
cards.text: Edit records.

cards.title: …-delete
cards.text: Delete records and restore them from the trash.

items: view-core and the application tabs (for example view-web, view-eshop) - without them you cannot get into the module at all.
core-view-welcome-page - the welcome page after signing in; recommended to keep always on.
view-deleted - access to the trash across modules.
Permissions to switch an application off and on (maintenance mode) and for the settings of applications have keys of their own at their applications.

blocks.content: The field Search permissions by name or key… narrows the list to the matching permissions.

steps.label: New role
steps.text: Press New role. A form opens.

steps.label: Role name
steps.text: Required, for example “Accountant”.

steps.label: Description
steps.text: An optional short description of the purpose of the role.

steps.label: Require 2FA for this role
steps.text: Tick it if everyone with this role must use two-factor authentication.

steps.label: Create role
steps.text: The role appears in the list - without permissions so far.

steps.label: Permissions
steps.text: Tick the permissions (chapter 04) and save.

sections.heading: 04. Setting the permissions of a role

items: Select the role in the list on the left.
Tick or untick permissions in the detail. The notice You have unsaved permission changes appears at the top.
Save permissions saves the changes; Discard returns to the saved state.

blocks.content: When you switch to another role with unsaved changes, the system asks whether you want to lose them.

Saved changes apply to all users with this role - at the latest within 20 minutes, at once after the page is reloaded in their browser. Permissions a user has on top of the role are set at the account on the Accounts page.

items: At the selected role press Edit name/description.
Change the name, the description or the option Require 2FA for this role.
Press Save.

blocks.content: Turning 2FA on for a role means everyone with the role enters a code from their e-mail when signing in and cannot turn it off.
Delete role and the confirmation Yes, delete remove the role permanently together with its permissions. The action cannot be undone.

items: A role assigned to at least one account cannot be deleted - give those accounts another role first.
The system role cannot be deleted.

blocks.content: The sysadmin role is a system role: it automatically has all permissions, always requires two-factor authentication and its name, description and permissions cannot be changed or deleted. In the detail it is marked with a notice and the checkboxes are locked. Accounts with the sysadmin role may be managed only by another sysadmin.

The Export button opens the export window: choose the format and the columns (role name, description, system role, enforced 2FA, number of users and the list of permissions). Useful as an overview of access for an audit or a review.

items: Give roles only the permissions people really need (principle of least privilege).
Rather several narrow roles than one wide role for everybody.
Entrust deleting and the trash (…-delete, view-deleted) and account management only to trusted people.
For roles with access to personal data or account management turn on mandatory 2FA.
Review the export of roles regularly and remove permissions that are no longer needed.

blocks.content: On this page you manage the accounts of everyone who signs in to the administration: you create new accounts, assign roles and permissions, and handle passwords, two-factor authentication, blocking, and deletion. This guide walks you through every function step by step - from creating an account to removing it permanently.

The most important rule: an administrator never enters or knows the password of a new account. The account is created without a password and the user sets it personally through the link in the activation e-mail.

sections.heading: 01. Who Can See the Page and What They Can Do

blocks.content: What you see on the page depends on your permissions. Buttons and menu items you have no permission for are not displayed at all - this is not an error. If a function described in this guide is missing for you, ask the administrator who manages your account to add the permission.

cards.title: Viewing the page
cards.text: Permission core-administrators-view. You see the accounts table, account details, filters, data export, and reports.

cards.title: Creating accounts
cards.text: Permission core-administrators-create. The action menu gains the item for creating a new record.

cards.title: Editing accounts
cards.text: Permission core-administrators-update. Each account row gains the actions for editing, changing the password, and resending the activation.

cards.title: Deleting accounts
cards.text: Permission core-administrators-delete. Each account row gains the delete action and the trash gains the option to delete permanently.

cards.title: Trash
cards.text: Permission view-deleted. The action menu gains the switch between active accounts and the trash.

cards.title: The sysadmin role
cards.text: Only a sysadmin sees the allowed e-mail domain settings, may force two-factor authentication on a specific account, and may work with accounts that have the sysadmin role.

sections.heading: 02. Finding Your Way Around the Page

cards.title: Action menu
cards.text: A drop-down menu above the table. It contains showing and hiding the filters, creating a record, data export, e-mail domains (sysadmin only), reports, and the switch between active accounts and the trash.

cards.title: Accounts table
cards.text: Each row is one account. Columns: ID, name, e-mail, role, whether the account is blocked, and the date of the last sign-in.

cards.title: Row actions
cards.text: Icons at the end of the row: magnifier (details), edit, key (password change), envelope (resend activation - only for accounts not yet activated), and delete.

cards.title: Filter panel
cards.text: A side panel opened from the action menu. It is used to search and sort accounts - see chapter 13.

cards.title: Pagination
cards.text: Below the table you switch pages and choose the number of records per page. The trash has its own independent pagination.

cards.title: Refreshing data
cards.text: Next to the table you see the time of the last update and a button for an immediate refresh. The data also refreshes automatically roughly every 15 minutes while the browser tab is open and active.

blocks.content: The heading above the table always shows whether you are looking at active accounts or at the trash. Bulk deletion of several accounts at once is intentionally disabled on this page - accounts are always deleted one at a time.
Every account goes through several states. Once you know which state an account is in, you also know which action to use.

steps.label: Created, pending activation
steps.text: The account exists but has no password. The user cannot sign in until a password is set through the link in the activation e-mail. The row offers the action for resending the activation.

steps.label: Active
steps.text: The user has set a password and can sign in. The resend-activation action disappears from the row.

steps.label: Blocked
steps.text: An optional and reversible state. The user is signed out immediately and cannot sign in until you remove the block. The account stays in the table.

steps.label: In the trash
steps.text: A deleted account moves to the trash. The user cannot sign in, but the account can be restored with all its settings.

steps.label: Permanently deleted
steps.text: The account is removed from the trash for good. This step cannot be undone.

sections.heading: 04. Creating a New Account Step by Step

steps.label: 1. Prepare the details
steps.text: Verify the exact e-mail address of the new user - the activation link is sent to it and it also serves as the sign-in name. Decide which role the user should get. If the system restricts e-mail domains (chapter 16), the address must belong to an allowed domain, otherwise the account cannot be created.

steps.label: 2. Open the form
steps.text: In the action menu above the table, choose the item for creating a record. The item is visible only in the active accounts view (not in the trash) and only if you have the permission to create accounts.

steps.label: 3. Read the notice
steps.text: An information banner appears above the form, reminding you that the account is created without a password. You do not enter a password - the form has no field for it.

steps.label: 4. Sign-in e-mail (required)
steps.text: Enter the e-mail in a valid format. Each e-mail can have only one account - if an account with this address already exists (even one lying in the trash), the system refuses to save.

steps.label: 5. Full name (required)
steps.text: The first and last name of the user. It is shown in the table, in the account details, and in the greeting of e-mails.

steps.label: 6. Role (required)
steps.text: Choose a role from the list. The role defines the basic set of permissions. The list shows only roles you are allowed to assign - those whose permissions you all hold yourself. The sysadmin role can be assigned only by a sysadmin.

steps.label: 7. Extra permissions (optional)
steps.text: After you choose a role, the permissions the role already contains are ticked and locked automatically in the permission list. By ticking others you give the user something beyond the role. Always choose the role first - every role change returns the permission selection to the default state of the new role.

steps.label: 8. Two-factor authentication (optional)
steps.text: Ticking it turns on verification by an e-mailed code at every sign-in. For roles that require two-factor authentication (always sysadmin, possibly other roles depending on their settings) the field is locked and the verification is always on for the account - it cannot be turned off.

steps.label: 9. Internal note (optional)
steps.text: Free text for administrators, for example the job position or the reason the account was created. Only the sysadmin and accounts with the permission for the list of administrators (core-administrators-view) see it - the account itself does not without that permission. Do not write sensitive personal data into it.

steps.label: 10. Save
steps.text: Confirm the form. A confirmation that the account was created appears, the form closes, and the new account shows up in the table.

steps.label: 11. What happens next
steps.text: The system immediately sends the activation e-mail to the user. The account is created but not yet active: it is not blocked, it just has no password. Tell the user to check the inbox, including the spam folder.

blocks.content: You cannot set account blocking or forced two-factor authentication for a specific account during creation - these fields are available only when editing an existing account (chapter 09).
If saving ends with a message about a disallowed e-mail domain, the address does not belong to the allowed domains. Ask a sysadmin to add an exception and then create the account again.
If saving ends with a message that you cannot assign a role granting permissions you do not have yourself, choose a different role or ask a sysadmin to create the account.

sections.heading: 05. Account Activation - What the New User Does

blocks.content: You can forward this chapter to the new user or guide them through it. Both the activation e-mail and the activation page are in English.

steps.label: 1. Opening the e-mail
steps.text: The e-mail greets the user by name, announces that an account has been created, and contains the button "Set password and activate". If the button does not work, the same link is below it, ready to be copied into the browser.

steps.label: 2. Link validity
steps.text: The link is valid for a limited time (the number of hours is stated in the e-mail) and can be used only once.

steps.label: 3. Link verification
steps.text: After the click the page briefly verifies the link. If it is fine, the form "Set your password" appears, with the e-mail of the account shown below the title.

steps.label: 4. Setting the password
steps.text: The user enters a new password and repeats it for confirmation. Below the first field the fulfilled password requirements are ticked off live. The eye icon shows or hides the password. If the two passwords do not match, the page says so and the form cannot be submitted.

steps.label: 5. Submitting
steps.text: The button "Set password and activate account" completes the activation. If the password does not meet the requirements, the page shows the reason and the password must be adjusted.

steps.label: 6. Done
steps.text: The page shows "Account activated" and redirects the user to the sign-in page after a few seconds (or the user can click "Go to sign in now"). The user is not signed in automatically - they sign in with their e-mail and the password they have just set.

cards.title: Password length
cards.text: 8 to 64 characters.

cards.title: Letter
cards.text: The password must contain at least one letter.

cards.title: Digit
cards.text: The password must contain at least one digit.

cards.title: Special character
cards.text: The password must contain at least one special character (for example an exclamation mark or a hyphen).

blocks.content: When the link has expired, has already been used, or is damaged, the page says the link cannot be used. The user cannot request a new link personally - they must ask an administrator, who resends the activation (chapter 06).
If someone received the activation e-mail and was not expecting an account, they can safely ignore the message - without clicking the link and setting a password nobody can sign in to the account.
The action with the envelope icon in the account row. It is visible only for accounts that have not been activated yet, and only if you have the permission to edit accounts.

cards.title: The e-mail did not arrive
cards.text: First have the user check the spam folder. Then verify the e-mail in the account is spelled correctly and resend the activation.

cards.title: The link expired
cards.text: The user did not manage to set the password while the link was valid. Resend the activation.

cards.title: The link cannot be used
cards.text: The link has already been opened and used once, or was damaged when copied. Resend the activation.

cards.title: You corrected the e-mail
cards.text: If the account was created with a typo in the address, first correct the e-mail by editing the account and then resend the activation - it will go to the correct address.

steps.label: 1. Find the account
steps.text: Find the account in the table, using the filter by name or e-mail if needed.

steps.label: 2. Click the envelope
steps.text: In the account row, click the resend-activation action.

steps.label: 3. Confirmation
steps.text: The system confirms that the activation e-mail has been resent.

steps.label: 4. The old link stops working
steps.text: The user must use the link from the newest e-mail. All activation links sent earlier are invalid from this moment.

blocks.content: For an account that is already activated, the system only states that the account is active and sends nothing. A forgotten password of an activated account is covered in chapter 11. If the e-mail fails to send, an error is shown - try again later and contact a sysadmin if the problem persists.

Every account has exactly one role. A role is a named set of permissions and determines what the user sees and may do in the administration. On top of the role, extra permissions can be added to an individual account - useful when one person exceptionally needs something the role does not contain. Roles themselves are not created or edited on this page; here you only assign them.

cards.title: Which roles I can assign
cards.text: Only roles whose permissions you all hold yourself. A role that would give someone more than you have is not shown in the list (when editing an account, its current role is shown as well). A sysadmin can assign any role.

cards.title: The sysadmin role
cards.text: Only a sysadmin may assign it to a new account, promote an existing account to it, or edit an account that has it.

cards.title: Which extra permissions I can give
cards.text: You may add or remove only permissions you hold yourself. If you tick a permission outside your reach, it is not saved. Permissions that someone with wider rights granted earlier and that you do not hold stay unchanged.

cards.title: Ticked and locked permissions
cards.text: These are the permissions contained in the role. They cannot be removed individually - they change only when the role changes.

cards.title: Your own account
cards.text: You cannot change your own role. If you need a different role, ask another authorised administrator.

steps.label: 1. Open the account for editing
steps.text: In the account row, click the edit action.

steps.label: 2. Choose the new role
steps.text: The permission list is recalculated immediately: previously selected extra permissions are cleared and only the permissions of the new role stay ticked.

steps.label: 3. Save
steps.text: The system shows a notice that all extra permissions were reset with the role change, and confirms the account update.

steps.label: 4. Add extra permissions if needed
steps.text: If the user needs something extra in the new role as well, open the account for editing again, tick the permissions, and save. This cannot be done in the same step as the role change.

blocks.content: A role change always removes all extra permissions. This is intentional - the user does not carry exceptions from the old role into the new one.

Two-factor authentication adds a second step to the password: after entering the e-mail and password, the user receives a one-time code by e-mail, without which the sign-in cannot be completed. Even if someone guesses or steals the password, they cannot get into the account without access to the mailbox.

cards.title: Optional
cards.text: The two-factor authentication checkbox in the account form can be turned on and off. This applies to accounts where the verification is not forced.

cards.title: Forced by the role
cards.text: The sysadmin role always has it on. Other roles may require it as well if a sysadmin configured them so. The field is then locked, the verification is always on for the account, and it cannot be turned off.

cards.title: Forced for a specific account
cards.text: When editing an account whose role does not require the verification, a sysadmin can tick the force field. The account then has the verification permanently on and only a sysadmin may turn it off again. Only a sysadmin sees this field, only when editing (not when creating), and only for roles that do not force the verification themselves.

steps.label: 1. E-mail and password
steps.text: The user signs in on the sign-in page with e-mail and password as usual.

steps.label: 2. The code arrives by e-mail
steps.text: A message with a six-digit verification code arrives at the e-mail of the account.

steps.label: 3. Entering the code
steps.text: The sign-in page shows a field for the code and a countdown of how long the code remains valid. After entering all six digits the user confirms the sign-in.

steps.label: 4. The code did not arrive or expired
steps.text: With the resend button the user requests a new code. The button becomes active 60 seconds after the last sending - until then a countdown runs next to it.

steps.label: 5. Going back
steps.text: With the back button the user returns to entering the e-mail and password, for example after signing in to the wrong account.

blocks.content: Never share the verification code with anyone. If a user receives a code without trying to sign in, someone knows their password - they should change it immediately.

After several failed sign-in attempts the sign-in page may additionally require a check that the visitor is not a robot. This is a standard protection; once the check passes, the sign-in completes normally.

steps.label: 1. Open the edit form
steps.text: In the account row, click the edit action. The action is visible only with the permission to edit accounts.

steps.label: 2. Check the pre-filled data
steps.text: The form opens with the current data of the account. The permission list shows the role permissions ticked (locked) as well as the extra permissions (changeable).

steps.label: 3. Change what you need
steps.text: Only fields that are not locked can be changed. The meaning of each field is described below.

steps.label: 4. Save
steps.text: After saving, a confirmation of the account update appears, the form closes, and the table refreshes. The cancel button closes the form without changes.

cards.title: E-mail
cards.text: Change of the sign-in e-mail. The address must be unique. The allowed-domain restriction is not checked when editing; it applies only to creating accounts.

cards.title: Full name
cards.text: Correction or change of the user name.

cards.title: Role and extra permissions
cards.text: See chapter 07. Remember that a role change removes the extra permissions.

cards.title: Two-factor authentication
cards.text: See chapter 08. For accounts with forced verification the field is locked.

cards.title: Forcing two-factor authentication
cards.text: Only a sysadmin sees the field, and only for accounts whose role does not force the verification itself.

cards.title: Blocking
cards.text: See chapter 10. For accounts with the sysadmin role the field is locked.

cards.title: Internal note
cards.text: Free text for administrators, visible in the account details.

blocks.content: An account with the sysadmin role may be edited only by a sysadmin. For everyone else the system refuses the edit and records the attempt.
Blocking is a fast and reversible way to cut off access immediately without deleting the account. The account stays in the table with all its settings.

cards.title: When to block
cards.text: When misuse of the account or a password leak is suspected, during a temporary absence of the user, or as the first step when a cooperation ends, before deletion is decided.

cards.title: What happens
cards.text: The user is signed out immediately on all devices and cannot sign in again while the block lasts.

cards.title: What cannot be blocked
cards.text: You cannot block your own account. Accounts with the sysadmin role can never be blocked - the field is locked for them.

cards.title: Unblocking
cards.text: Edit the account, untick the block, and save. The user then signs in with the original password.

steps.label: 1. Open the account for editing
steps.text: Blocking is set only when editing an existing account; it is not available during creation.

steps.label: 2. Tick the block
steps.text: Tick the field for blocking the account.

steps.label: 3. Save
steps.text: The block applies immediately after saving.

steps.label: 4. Verify the result
steps.text: The blocked column in the table shows that the account is blocked. Use the blocked filter to list all blocked accounts.

sections.heading: 11. Passwords - Forgotten Password and Password Change

blocks.content: A password can be handled in three ways. Choose according to the situation:

cards.title: The user forgot the password
cards.text: The user resets the password personally from the sign-in page. This is the recommended way - nobody else knows the new password and the administrator does not need to do anything.

cards.title: An administrator must change the password
cards.text: Use it when the user cannot reach their mailbox, or when the password must be changed immediately (for example when a leak is suspected). You change the password with the key icon action.

cards.title: The account was never activated
cards.text: Such an account has no password yet. Do not handle it with a password change - resend the activation e-mail (chapter 06).

blocks.content: Forgotten password - what the user does:

steps.label: 1. The link on the sign-in page
steps.text: Next to the password field the user clicks the forgotten-password link. A small window opens.

steps.label: 2. Entering the e-mail
steps.text: The user enters the e-mail of the account and submits the request. The window confirms the sending and closes itself after a moment.

steps.label: 3. The e-mail with the link
steps.text: A message with the button "Reset your password" arrives in the mailbox. The link is valid for a limited time (the number of minutes is stated in the e-mail) and can be used only once. If the user did not request the reset, they ignore the message - the password stays unchanged.

steps.label: 4. The new password
steps.text: On the page "Set a new password" the user enters the new password and repeats it. The same requirements apply as during activation: 8 to 64 characters, a letter, a digit, and a special character. The button "Set new password" becomes active only when the password meets all requirements and both fields match.

steps.label: 5. Confirmation
steps.text: The page shows "Password changed" and redirects the user to the sign-in page after a moment.

steps.label: 6. Invalid link
steps.text: If the link has expired or has already been used, the page says so after the form is submitted. The user returns to the sign-in page and requests the reset again.

blocks.content: Password change by an administrator - procedure:

steps.label: 1. Click the key
steps.text: In the account row, click the action with the key icon. The action is visible only with the permission to edit accounts.

steps.label: 2. Check the account
steps.text: The form title contains the e-mail of the account whose password you are changing. Make sure it is the right account.

steps.label: 3. Enter YOUR current password
steps.text: The first field confirms that it is really you making the change. Enter your own sign-in password - not the password of the user whose password you are changing.

steps.label: 4. Enter the new password
steps.text: Enter the new password and repeat it for confirmation. It must have 8 to 64 characters and contain a letter, a digit, and a special character.

steps.label: 5. Save
steps.text: The system confirms that the password has been changed. If you entered your own password in the first field incorrectly, the change is not made and an error is shown.

steps.label: 6. Hand over the password safely
steps.text: Tell the user the new password in a safe way (in person or by phone, not by e-mail) and ask them to change it to their own as soon as possible.

blocks.content: After every password change the account owner receives an e-mail notification with the date and time of the change. If neither the owner nor an administrator acting on their request made the change, the owner should report it immediately - in that case block the account (chapter 10) and change the password. With many password changes in a short time the system may temporarily stop sending further notifications.
The password of an account with the sysadmin role may be changed only by its owner or by another sysadmin.
The action with the magnifier icon in the row opens an overview of all data of the account. The details are read-only - nothing can be changed there - and you close them with the close button.

cards.title: Basic data
cards.text: Account ID, full name, and sign-in e-mail.

cards.title: Role and extra permissions
cards.text: The assigned role and the list of permissions the account received beyond the role.

cards.title: Account state
cards.text: Whether the account is blocked and the activation date. An empty activation date means the user has not set a password yet.

cards.title: Two-factor authentication
cards.text: Whether the verification is on for the account and whether a sysadmin forced it for this account.

cards.title: Internal note
cards.text: The text administrators wrote for the account.

cards.title: Created and updated dates
cards.text: When the account was created and when it was last modified.

steps.label: 1. Open the filters
steps.text: In the action menu choose the filters item. A side panel opens next to the table. The same item (its label changes to hiding the filters) closes the panel again.

steps.label: 2. Enter the conditions
steps.text: You can filter by name and e-mail (a part of the text is enough), by role (chosen from a list), and by whether the account is blocked (yes or no). Conditions can be combined.

steps.label: 3. Choose the sorting
steps.text: In the panel you choose the column to sort the table by and the direction. The default order is from the newest account.

steps.label: 4. Apply the filters
steps.text: After confirming, the table reloads with matching accounts only. The filters stay in effect when you move to another page and when you change the number of records per page.

steps.label: 5. Clear the filters
steps.text: The clear-filters button returns you to the complete list in the default order.

blocks.content: Tip: the search above the table looks in the name and the e-mail. It does not search by role - use the role filter for that.

cards.title: Data export
cards.text: The export item in the action menu downloads the table of active accounts as a CSV file that you can open in a spreadsheet program. Roles and permissions are not part of the export. The export is available only in the active accounts view, not in the trash.

cards.title: Handling the export
cards.text: The file contains personal data (names and e-mails). Store it only in places intended for work data, do not send it outside the company, and delete it after use.

cards.title: Reports
cards.text: The reports item opens the chart builder for accounts. You can see how many accounts are blocked, how many have two-factor authentication turned on, and how many have it forced, by the date the account was created. Close the tool with its close button.

sections.heading: 15. Deleting an Account, Trash, Restore, and Permanent Deletion

blocks.content: Deletion has two levels. A regular delete only moves the account to the trash, from which it can be brought back. Only permanent deletion from the trash is final.

steps.label: 1. Deleting to the trash
steps.text: In the account row, click the delete action (requires the permission to delete accounts). The account disappears from the active accounts table and moves to the trash. The deleted user can no longer sign in.

steps.label: 2. Viewing the trash
steps.text: In the action menu switch to the trash (requires the permission to view deleted records). The heading above the table changes and the table shows the ID, name, e-mail, and deletion date. In the trash view the action menu does not offer creating a record or exporting.

steps.label: 3. Restoring an account
steps.text: The restore action in the trash row returns the account to the active ones with all its original settings. The user can sign in again.

steps.label: 4. Permanent deletion
steps.text: The permanent delete action in the trash removes the account for good (requires the permission to delete accounts). This step cannot be undone.

steps.label: 5. Returning to active accounts
steps.text: The same item in the action menu (its label changes to showing the active ones) takes you back.

cards.title: Your own account
cards.text: You cannot delete the account you are currently signed in with.

cards.title: Sysadmin accounts
cards.text: An account with the sysadmin role may be deleted and restored from the trash only by another sysadmin. Deleting an account (also to the trash) signs it out on every device at once. When the trash is emptied in bulk, sysadmin accounts stay in the trash unless a sysadmin is emptying it.

cards.title: The e-mail of a trashed account is taken
cards.text: While an account lies in the trash, a new account with the same e-mail cannot be created. Either restore the account from the trash, or permanently delete it first.

cards.title: Block or delete?
cards.text: If the user may come back or you are not sure, block the account. Use deletion when the account will no longer be needed.

blocks.content: A sysadmin can define which e-mail addresses new accounts may be created with - typically only the company domain. Open the settings with the e-mail domains item in the action menu; only a sysadmin sees this item.

cards.title: Primary domain
cards.text: The basic company domain, for example company.com. Once filled in, accounts can be created and can log in only with addresses from this domain or from the exceptions below - for every role, sysadmin included.

cards.title: No restriction
cards.text: If you leave the primary domain empty and save, the restriction is turned off and an account can be created with any e-mail.

cards.title: Domain exception
cards.text: Another whole domain accounts may be created with - for example the domain of a partner company.

cards.title: E-mail exception
cards.text: One specific address outside the allowed domains - for example an external collaborator with a private e-mail.

steps.label: 1. Setting the primary domain
steps.text: Type the domain into the primary domain field and click the save button next to the field. The system confirms the save. The primary domain is saved only with this button.

steps.label: 2. Adding an exception
steps.text: In the add-exception part choose the type (domain or e-mail), type the value, and click the add button or press Enter. The exception is saved immediately and appears in the corresponding list. Enter values in lower case.

steps.label: 3. Checking the lists
steps.text: The window shows two lists: allowed domains and allowed e-mails. An empty list is marked with a text saying nothing is in it yet.

steps.label: 4. Removing an exception
steps.text: The cross next to an item removes the exception. The removal applies immediately: accounts that are no longer allowed are logged out at once and cannot log in - this applies to every role, sysadmin included. A change that would block you yourself is not saved; add an exception for your own e-mail first.

steps.label: 5. Closing the window
steps.text: Close the window with the close button, the cross in the corner, or by clicking outside the window. The window cannot be closed while the primary domain is being saved.

blocks.content: The restriction applies only to creating new accounts. Existing accounts stay unchanged even if their e-mail does not match the allowed domains, and the restriction is not checked when the e-mail of an existing account is edited either. An attempt to create an account with a disallowed address is refused and recorded as a security event.

sections.heading: 17. Fixed Rules That Cannot Be Bypassed

blocks.content: The following rules protect the system against mistakes and misuse. They always apply, regardless of permissions, and are not an application error.

cards.title: Sysadmin accounts are managed only by a sysadmin
cards.text: Creating, editing, promoting to sysadmin, changing the password of someone else with the sysadmin role, and deleting such an account are reserved for the sysadmin role.

cards.title: A sysadmin always has two-factor authentication
cards.text: The verification cannot be turned off for the sysadmin role.

cards.title: A sysadmin cannot be blocked
cards.text: Nobody can block an account with the sysadmin role, not even another sysadmin.

cards.title: You cannot block or delete yourself
cards.text: Your own account cannot be blocked or deleted, and you cannot change your own role.

cards.title: Nobody gives away more than they have
cards.text: A role or an extra permission cannot be assigned if the target account would gain a permission you do not have yourself. The sysadmin is the exception.

cards.title: One e-mail, one account
cards.text: Two accounts with the same e-mail cannot exist, including accounts in the trash.

cards.title: Everything is recorded
cards.text: Creations, edits, password changes, blocks, deletions, restores, and refused attempts are stored in the system records, including who performed the action.

cards.title: A new user did not receive the activation e-mail
cards.text: Have the spam folder checked, verify the e-mail in the account is correct, and resend the activation (chapter 06).

cards.title: The activation link does not work
cards.text: The link has expired or has already been used. Resend the activation and tell the user to use the newest e-mail.

cards.title: A user forgot the password
cards.text: Point them to the forgotten-password link on the sign-in page. Only if that is not possible, change the password yourself (chapter 11).

cards.title: A user is not receiving the verification code
cards.text: Have the spam folder checked and the code requested again after 60 seconds. If the verification is not forced, it can be turned off temporarily by editing the account.

cards.title: Suspected misuse of an account
cards.text: Block the account immediately - the user is signed out everywhere. Then change the password, investigate the situation, and only then unblock the account.

cards.title: A user is leaving the company
cards.text: Block the account or delete it to the trash on the day of departure. Once it is certain the account will not be needed again, delete it from the trash permanently.

cards.title: I cannot see a button or menu item
cards.text: You lack the relevant permission (chapter 01), or the action makes no sense for the account - for example resending the activation for an activated account.

cards.title: A role is missing from the list
cards.text: The role contains a permission you do not have yourself, so you may not assign it. Ask a sysadmin.

cards.title: The account cannot be created because of the domain
cards.text: The e-mail does not belong to the allowed domains. Ask a sysadmin for a domain exception or an exception for the specific e-mail (chapter 16).

cards.title: An account with this e-mail already exists
cards.text: Look the account up with the e-mail filter among the active accounts. If it is not there, check the trash - either restore the account or delete it permanently.

cards.title: A field in the form cannot be changed
cards.text: The field is locked by a rule: two-factor authentication on forced accounts, blocking on sysadmin accounts, permissions contained in the role.

cards.title: An error appeared that I do not understand
cards.text: Try the action again. If the error persists, report it to the system administrator and describe what you were doing and with which account.

blocks.content: A final word: accounts contain personal data and open access to the whole administration. Create them only for people who really need them, assign the lowest role that is sufficient for the work, block or delete accounts that are no longer needed, and never share passwords or verification codes.

The system log is the unchangeable history of what happened in Core: who signed in and out when, who created, edited or deleted an account, a role or a legal document, who exported what and which actions the system refused. It serves for checking, for tracing errors and as evidence for an audit.
Log entries cannot be edited or deleted by hand. Old entries are deleted only by the nightly clean-up according to the retention set in Legal documents → Data retention.

cards.title: ID
cards.text: The sequence number of the entry.

cards.title: Time
cards.text: When the event happened.

cards.title: User
cards.text: Who performed the action (e-mail). System actions have no user.

cards.title: Action
cards.text: The type of the event - for example Created, Updated, Soft deleted, Permanently deleted, Restored, Login, Failed login, Logout, Password changed, Exported, Error.

cards.title: Module
cards.text: Which part the event concerns: Authentication, Users, Roles, Legal documents, Core (general).

cards.title: Event description
cards.text: A human-readable description of what happened.

cards.title: IP address / origin
cards.text: Where the action came from.

blocks.content: Actions ending with denied (for example Update denied) mean someone tried the action but the system refused it - typically because of a missing permission.

items: In the Actions menu choose Filters.
Filter by ID, user or e-mail, action type, module or IP address. Choose the order in Sort by.
Press Apply filters.

blocks.content: Who deleted an account? - action Soft deleted, module Users. Who signed in at night? - action Login and sorting by time. What did a particular user do? - filter User.

The Details icon shows all data of the entry: time, IP address, event type, module, the detailed description, the table and ID of the affected record, the ID and e-mail of the user and the technical data (JSON) - for example which values changed.

You can export the log (Actions → export data) and evaluate it in charts (Actions → generate charts and reports) - for example the number of sign-ins over time or the breakdown of action types. The procedure is in the introductory chapter.

The log contains e-mails and IP addresses - these are personal data. Protect exported files and delete them after use. Personal data of customers, applicants, inquiries and other records is not stored in the log: in the changes and in the copy of the submitted form the value shows as [masked] - the log tells that a field changed, not its content.

The page requires the permission View the core log (core-logs-view) - the log holds the e-mail and IP addresses of every account, so not everybody who sees the Core section has it. A failed sign-in names the e-mail only for an existing account; any other typed text (a typo, a password typed by mistake) is written only as “unknown account” with a code it cannot be read back from. The logs of the individual applications (website, e-shop, project portal) have their own pages in those applications.

Security monitoring records suspicious activity: failed sign-ins, password guessing, wrong verification codes, robots on forms, exceeded limits, automated scans and blocked content on the pages. For every entry the system explains in plain words what happened and what it recommends doing.

The page has two tabs: Events (the table of entries, opens first) and Overview (the activity chart and the retention setting). The chosen tab is in the page address, so it survives a reload and the Back button.
Most entries are harmless - the internet is full of robots trying common addresses. What matters is watching critical entries and entries whose count grows quickly.

sections.heading: 01. Chart of the volume of suspicious activity

blocks.content: The Overview tab shows a bar chart of the last 14 days. Each bar is one day split by severity (Critical, Warning, Info). Hover to see the counts, click a bar to open the Events tab with the table filtered to the entries of that day.

cards.title: Last seen
cards.text: The time of the last occurrence.

cards.title: Event type
cards.text: What happened (list in chapter 03).

cards.title: Severity
cards.text: Info, Warning or Critical.

cards.title: IP address
cards.text: Where the activity came from.

cards.title: Occurrences
cards.text: How many times the same event repeated from the same address - repetitions do not add new rows.

cards.title: Status
cards.text: New, Reviewed, False positive or Confirmed attack.

blocks.content: Filter the table by ID, event type, severity, status and IP address. The details of an entry also show the browser (User-Agent), the address and method of the request, the user ID, the first and last occurrence, the note and the technical context.

cards.title: Failed login attempt
cards.text: A wrong password for an account. Common on its own (a typo).

cards.title: Suspected brute-force attack
cards.text: Repeated failed sign-ins to one account - from then on the system requires CAPTCHA. Check that the account does not have a weak password.

cards.title: CAPTCHA failure
cards.text: A sign-in or a public form without a valid check that it is not a robot.

cards.title: CAPTCHA service outage
cards.text: The external verification service did not answer - usually a temporary outage, not an attack. For forms, visitors cannot send them during the outage.

cards.title: Honeypot – bot caught
cards.text: A robot filled in a hidden field of a form. Nothing was saved or sent.

cards.title: Request rate limit exceeded
cards.text: Too many requests from one address in a minute (for example an attempt to flood a form).

cards.title: Invalid verification code (2FA)
cards.text: After a correct password a wrong code was entered. Repeatedly = someone may know the password.

cards.title: 2FA code attempts / resend requests exhausted
cards.text: The number of attempts or new codes in one sign-in was exceeded.

cards.title: Invalid login token
cards.text: An attempt to renew a sign-in with an expired or invalid token - usually just an expired sign-in.

cards.title: Reused login token (possible theft)
cards.text: Critical. The same sign-in was used from two places. The system ended all sign-ins of the account - check with the user and have them change the password.

cards.title: Automated vulnerability scan
cards.text: A robot tried addresses typical for vulnerabilities of other systems. Such addresses do not exist in this system.

cards.title: Blocked by the security policy (CSP)
cards.text: A visitor's browser blocked a script or resource that is not allowed. Often caused by browser extensions; a repeated foreign domain may mean an attempt to inject malicious code.

steps.label: Triage
steps.text: Press Triage in the row of the entry. A window opens with the explanation What happened and Recommended action.

steps.label: Status
steps.text: Choose Reviewed (checked, nothing more needed), False positive (it was not an attack) or Confirmed attack.

steps.label: Note
steps.text: Optionally write what you found - for example “the IP belongs to a business partner”.

steps.label: Save
steps.text: The status is saved. False positive is first confirmed in a dialog - the entry then no longer counts as active suspicious activity.

blocks.content: New entries are also shown in the calendar in the panel Waiting for you. Evaluate them regularly so that the overview stays clean and real attacks do not get lost.

sections.heading: 05. What to do in a real attack

items: An attack on a specific account (brute force, wrong 2FA codes, reused token): contact the user, have them change the password, turn on or enforce 2FA, or block the account temporarily.
A lasting flood from one IP address: ask the technical administration to block the address at the firewall, hosting or CDN level. The administration itself does not block IP addresses.
Repeated CSP entries with a domain the website really uses (new analytics, a payment gateway): pass them to the developers to allow it in the security policy.
Mark the entry as Confirmed attack and write in the note what you did.

blocks.content: The entries contain IP addresses, so they are deleted automatically. In the retention card of the Overview tab set after how many days entries are deleted (7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 180 or 365 days) and save with Save retention. The clean-up runs every night.

items: Clean up old records now - after a confirmation it permanently deletes entries older than the set period at once. When there are none, nothing is deleted - that is fine.
Delete in a row - permanently deletes one entry.

blocks.content: Deleting security entries cannot be undone. Do not delete entries that may serve as evidence of an attack.

blocks.content: The Applications page shows all applications you can manage (website, e-shop, project portal …), their current status and a simple diagnosis. With the permission you switch an application off into maintenance mode and on again from here.

Every signed-in user sees the page; the card of an application is shown only to someone with the permission for the application tab and at least one of its pages. If you have access to no application, the page says so.

cards.title: Online (green)
cards.text: The public part runs and all is well.

cards.title: Online · problem (orange)
cards.text: It runs, but reported errors or a slow response in the last 24 hours - check the logs of the application.

cards.title: Offline · maintenance (red)
cards.text: The public part is switched off - visitors see the maintenance page.

cards.title: Unavailable
cards.text: The data of the application could not be read - a server problem; contact technical support.

cards.title: Data response
cards.text: How fast the server answered (in milliseconds). Units to hundreds of ms are normal.

cards.title: Entries in 24 h
cards.text: The number of entries in the log of the application in the last 24 hours - shows the load.

cards.title: Errors in 24 h
cards.text: The number of errors in the last 24 hours.

cards.title: Last activity / Last error
cards.text: When something last happened in the application and when the last error occurred.

blocks.content: The status and diagnosis refresh by themselves every 10 seconds while the page is open and the browser tab is active. Refresh status loads them at once; the time of the last check is next to the button.
The Manage button of an application opens its first page you may open. You can also switch between applications with the Applications button in the header.

sections.heading: 04. Switching an application off and on (maintenance mode)

steps.label: Switch application off
steps.text: At the application press Switch application off (the button is also in the header of the application dashboard).

steps.label: Administrator verification
steps.text: The window shows the new state OFFLINE – MAINTENANCE MODE and what will happen. Enter your current password.

steps.label: Confirm and save
steps.text: The public part switches off and visitors see the maintenance page with the logo, a short notice, contacts and a language switch. The administration keeps running.

steps.label: Switch application on
steps.text: The same steps switch the application on - state ONLINE – NORMAL OPERATION. A visitor on the maintenance page returns to the website once they open or reload it.

blocks.content: Switching an application off immediately takes its public part offline for all visitors (for example the e-shop takes no orders, clients cannot get into the portal). Use it only for the time strictly necessary and do not forget to switch the application on again.
Only accounts with the maintenance permission of the application see the button. Every change of the state is written to the log of the application.
The Releases page shows which version of the system is running and what changed in every release - in the core (Core) and in the applications you can manage.
Every signed-in user sees the page. The texts of the changes are in English.

sections.heading: 01. Running version and the list of releases

items: At the top is the running version in the form vYYYY.MM.N (year, month, the number of the release in the month), for example v2026.11.3.
Releases are sorted from the newest. The newest is expanded; click a release to expand or collapse it. The running release is marked Running; each shows its number of changes.

cards.title: Type
cards.text: Security, Added, Changed, Fixed or Removed.

cards.title: Part
cards.text: The core or the name of an application; the mark public part means a change visitors see.

cards.title: Description
cards.text: A short description of the change, sometimes with a ticket number (for example #57) under which it was reported.

blocks.content: The buttons above the list (All, the core, the individual applications) show only the changes of the chosen part. You see only the core and the applications you have access to.

After an update the bar “Updated to … - N change(s) here” appears above the admin pages - only in the part you work in and only when the update changed it (an update of the e-shop does not disturb you on the website). What's new opens this page filtered to that part, Close hides the bar until the next update.
Developers write the release notes together with every change. A release without notes cannot be deployed, so the list is always complete.
